goal:
Orchestrator Prompt: agcli Parity & Superset vs btcli + Bittensor SDK

Mission: Achieve complete functional parity with btcli and the Bittensor Python SDK, then exceed them on coverage, agent-friendliness, and fault tolerance. Every capability must be validated against a real local subtensor chain (Docker), not mocked unit tests alone.

North star: For every workflow an operator can do with btcli or bittensor Python, there is an agcli path that works on localnet, produces equivalent on-chain effects, and is easier to script (--batch, --yes, --output json, --dry-run, structured errors, spending limits).

Non-negotiable constraints:
- Localnet is mandatory for write-path validation. Unit/CLI-parse tests alone do not count as covered.
- Chain effects are the source of truth. Compare storage/events/balances before and after — not just exit codes or stdout shape.
- Use the existing agcli harness: image ghcr.io/opentensor/subtensor-localnet:devnet-ready, `agcli localnet scaffold --output json`, existing suites tests/e2e_test.rs, tests/user_flows_e2e.rs, tests/localnet_e2e_test.rs
- Pin reference tool versions (btcli + bittensor from PyPI or git SHA) and record them in the parity matrix.
- Do not skip btcli. Even where agcli claims superset, run the btcli command on the same chain state to confirm equivalence.
- Out of scope (unless explicitly mapped): Miner/validator application runtime (Axon/Dendrite HTTP servers, Yuma math, subnet-specific scoring). Focus on chain operations the CLI/SDK expose.

Phase 0 — Environment bootstrap (cargo build --release, docker pull localnet image, python venv with bittensor-cli and bittensor, agcli localnet scaffold; scaffold variants A-E).
Phase 1 — Exhaustive inventory (btcli command tree + Bittensor SDK chain-relevant APIs).
Phase 2 — agcli cross-reference (per-row status COVERED_E2E | COVERED_CLI_ONLY | COVERED_UNIQUE | GAP | N/A).
Phase 3 — Localnet parity test suite (tests/parity/ with btcli/SDK + agcli runs and on-chain assertions).
Phase 4 — Gap closure (implement GAPs, add localnet tests, update docs, re-run reference tools).
Phase 5 — UX & fault-tolerance scorecard vs btcli.
Phase 6 — CI parity-localnet job + parity-report.md.

Definition of done: 100% btcli mapped+localnet-verified, 100% SDK extrinsic helpers mapped, zero COVERED_CLI_ONLY for writes, agcli UX >= btcli, all e2e suites pass.

Reference repos: https://github.com/opentensor/bittensor and https://github.com/latent-to/btcli .

Agent rules: one matrix row per PR for gap-closure, never mock chain for sign-off, use scaffold manifest for keys, document flag differences, use tests/e2e_modules/harness.rs patterns for flakiness.
summary: achieve btcli + Bittensor SDK parity (and superset) for agcli on real localnet; 6 phases, scaffold variants A-E, matrix-driven gap closure
acceptanceCriteria: docs/parity/versions.json pins agcli git SHA, btcli PyPI version + git SHA, bittensor PyPI version + git SHA, subtensor localnet image digest, rustc, docker.
examples/scaffold-variants/ contains scaffold configs A-E, each booting `agcli localnet scaffold --config <path> --output json` to a healthy state.
docs/parity/inventory-btcli.{md,json} enumerates every btcli subcommand with args + on-chain extrinsic.
docs/parity/inventory-sdk.{md,json} enumerates every chain-relevant bittensor SDK helper (extrinsic submitters + read helpers).
docs/parity/matrix.json contains one row per btcli command + per SDK extrinsic helper + per agcli-unique command, with `agcli_status` in {COVERED_E2E, COVERED_CLI_ONLY, COVERED_UNIQUE, GAP, N/A}.
tests/parity/ contains real-localnet tests for every COVERED_E2E and COVERED_UNIQUE row that touches chain state.
Every Phase 4 gap-fix worker opens its own draft PR (`openPR: true`, one matrix row per PR) and updates matrix.json from GAP to COVERED_E2E in that PR.
docs/parity/ux-scorecard.md compares agcli vs btcli on --batch, --dry-run, --yes, --output json, structured errors, spending limits, preflight errors, password handling, exit codes.
`.github/workflows/parity-localnet.yml` runs the parity suite against the pinned localnet image on every push to a parity-* branch.
docs/parity/parity-report.md states the final pass/fail against the mission-level definition of done.

tasks.name: bootstrap-toolchain
tasks.scopedGoal:
Phase 0a — Install toolchain, build agcli release, capture version manifest. (Narrow slice of Phase 0; the scaffold variants are a separate task.)

Read `.orchestrate/agcli-parity/discovery.md` FIRST (especially the `Cloud-agent VM environment recipe` section).

Do ONLY these things and write a handoff as soon as the deliverables exist. Do NOT try to also write scaffold variants or run the full Phase 0; that is `scaffold-variants-a-to-e`'s job.

1. `rustup install stable && rustup default stable` → verify `rustc -V` shows >= 1.89.
2. `git submodule update --init --depth=1 -- subtensor` → verify `subtensor/Cargo.toml` exists.
3. Install Docker (`sudo apt-get install -y docker.io`) with the vfs storage driver (see recipe). Start dockerd in the background (write `/tmp/dockerd.log`). Verify `sudo docker run --rm hello-world` succeeds.
4. `sudo docker pull ghcr.io/opentensor/subtensor-localnet:devnet-ready` → capture the first entry of the image's RepoDigests via `sudo docker inspect ghcr.io/opentensor/subtensor-localnet:devnet-ready --format <Go-template that prints the first RepoDigest>` (the Go template is two curly braces, the word `index`, a space, a dot, the word `RepoDigests`, a space, the number zero, two curly braces — write it directly in the shell).
5. `python3 -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate && pip install --upgrade pip && pip install bittensor bittensor-cli` → capture `pip show bittensor` and `pip show bittensor-cli` outputs (versions). Also capture `btcli --version`. **Do NOT** keep the venv alive between shells; just record the install ran clean.
6. `SKIP_METADATA_FETCH=1 cargo build --release --bin agcli` → verify `target/release/agcli --version` prints. Capture `git rev-parse HEAD` for the agcli git SHA.
7. Smoke-test the default scaffold: pick an unused port (e.g. 9970), run `sudo target/release/agcli localnet scaffold --output json --port 9970` (you may need `sudo` so Docker is reachable; alternatively add the agent user to the docker group). Capture the JSON; assert it contains `endpoint`, `block_height`, and at least one `subnets[0].neurons[0].ss58`. Tear down the container (`sudo docker rm -f agcli_localnet`).
8. Write `docs/parity/versions.json` and `docs/parity/versions.md` capturing:
   - `agcli`: `{ git_sha, version, build: "cargo --release" }`
   - `btcli`: `{ pypi_version, command: "pip install bittensor-cli==<version>" }` (best-effort git SHA via `pip show bittensor-cli` Homepage)
   - `bittensor`: same shape
   - `subtensor_localnet_image`: `{ tag: "ghcr.io/opentensor/subtensor-localnet:devnet-ready", digest: "sha256:..." }`
   - `subtensor_submodule_sha`: from `git -C subtensor rev-parse HEAD`
   - `rustc`, `docker`, `python` versions
   - `recorded_at`: UTC ISO timestamp
9. Append ONE line to `.orchestrate/agcli-parity/discovery.md` (at the `## Verified at` tail): `verified at <UTC iso> on rustc <ver>, docker <ver>, btcli <ver>, bittensor <ver>, agcli <git sha>, localnet image digest <sha256:...>`.
10. Commit and push to the cloud-agent branch (whatever the spawn assigned, which will be `orch/agcli-parity/bootstrap-toolchain`). No PR.

Known gotchas:
- The cloud-agent VM has no Docker preinstalled. Install yourself.
- `cargo build --release` is slow (4–10 minutes); be patient. Always set `SKIP_METADATA_FETCH=1`.
- If a step has been done before by a previous attempt on this branch (idempotent: `cargo build` is a no-op on warm cache), still record the artifact and continue.
- If you need >1 hour total, stop and produce a `partial` handoff with the deliverables you DID complete and a clear `## Notes` line about what remains. The planner will follow up. DO NOT silently quit.
- DO NOT also write the 5 scaffold variant TOMLs in this task. That is `scaffold-variants-a-to-e`'s scope and the planner will only schedule it after this handoff lands.

Do NOT touch src/, tests/, examples/scaffold-variants/, or any inventory/matrix/report file.
acceptance: rustc >= 1.89 installed.
subtensor submodule populated.
Docker installed and running; `sudo docker run --rm hello-world` succeeded.
`ghcr.io/opentensor/subtensor-localnet:devnet-ready` image pulled and digest recorded.
`bittensor` and `bittensor-cli` installed in `.venv/`; versions captured.
`SKIP_METADATA_FETCH=1 cargo build --release --bin agcli` succeeded.
`target/release/agcli localnet scaffold --output json --port <unused>` produced valid JSON with a non-empty `subnets[0].neurons[0].ss58`.
`docs/parity/versions.{json,md}` exists and pins agcli git SHA, btcli + bittensor versions, image digest, rustc/docker/python versions.
`.orchestrate/agcli-parity/discovery.md` has the final `verified at ...` line appended.

tasks.name: scaffold-variants-a-to-e
tasks.scopedGoal:
Phase 0b — Write 5 scaffold variant TOMLs at `examples/scaffold-variants/` and verify each boots cleanly via `agcli localnet scaffold --config <path> --output json --port <unused>`.

Read `.orchestrate/agcli-parity/discovery.md` FIRST. The `bootstrap-toolchain` handoff (pasted into your prompt automatically) confirms Rust/Docker/agcli/bittensor are already installed on this VM, so reuse them; do NOT reinstall.

Deliverables:

1. `examples/scaffold-variants/scaffold-A-baseline.toml` — 1 subnet, 3 neurons (1 validator + 2 miners), `commit_reveal = false`, `tempo = 100`, default-ish hyperparams. Container name `agcli_parity_A`. Port 9971.
2. `examples/scaffold-variants/scaffold-B-commit-reveal.toml` — 1 subnet, 3 neurons, `commit_reveal = true`, short reveal interval (set `reveal_period_epochs` to the lowest valid value the chain accepts; check `src/scaffold.rs` and `subtensor/pallets/admin-utils/src/lib.rs` for the canonical field). Container name `agcli_parity_B`. Port 9972.
3. `examples/scaffold-variants/scaffold-C-multi-subnet.toml` — 2 subnets with distinct tempos (e.g. 100 and 50), distinct `max_allowed_validators`. Each subnet has its own neuron set (validator + 2 miners). Container name `agcli_parity_C`. Port 9973.
4. `examples/scaffold-variants/scaffold-D-mechanisms.toml` — 1 subnet with `mechanism_count > 1`. Look up the field name in `src/scaffold.rs` (search for `mechanism`). If the scaffold TOML schema does NOT expose it directly, write the TOML as a baseline plus a top-of-file comment block giving the exact `agcli admin set-mechanism-count` or `sudo_set_mechanism_count` invocation to apply post-scaffold; document this in your handoff `## Findings`. Container name `agcli_parity_D`. Port 9974.
5. `examples/scaffold-variants/scaffold-E-user-liquidity.toml` — 1 subnet with user liquidity enabled (`toggle_user_liquidity` true). Same approach as Variant D if the field isn't in the TOML schema: comment block with the post-scaffold invocation. Container name `agcli_parity_E`. Port 9975.

For each variant:
- Boot via `sudo target/release/agcli localnet scaffold --config examples/scaffold-variants/scaffold-<X>-*.toml --output json --port <variant_port>` (one variant at a time; tear down between with `sudo docker rm -f <container_name>`).

- Capture the JSON output to `examples/scaffold-variants/scaffold-<X>-expected.json` so downstream parity tests have a stable reference.
- Tear down before booting the next variant.

Also write a single-line comment header at the top of each TOML stating: container name, port, expected subnet count, expected neuron count, any required post-scaffold sudo call.

Commit and push to the cloud-agent branch (`orch/agcli-parity/scaffold-variants-a-to-e`). No PR.

Known gotchas:
- Docker is reachable via `sudo`; either prefix commands or add the agent user to the `docker` group at the start.
- Variants D and E may require post-scaffold sudo calls if the TOML schema doesn't expose those fields. That is acceptable; document the call in the TOML comment and your handoff. Do NOT modify `src/scaffold.rs` to add the field — that's a downstream gap-closure task, log it as a follow-up.
- Use distinct ports per variant so a future parallel CI job can run them concurrently if needed.

Do NOT touch src/, tests/, docs/parity/inventory-*, docs/parity/matrix.*, docs/parity/ux-scorecard.md, or docs/parity/parity-report.md.

tasks.name: inventory-btcli
tasks.scopedGoal:
Phase 1 — Exhaustive enumeration of every btcli subcommand for the parity matrix.

Read `.orchestrate/agcli-parity/discovery.md` and the upstream `bootstrap-parity-env` handoff FIRST. You should already have a `.venv/` with `bittensor-cli` installed; if not, recreate it per the discovery recipe.

Deliverables:

1. `docs/parity/inventory-btcli.json` — array of rows, one per btcli subcommand. Each row:
   - `id`: e.g. `btcli.wallet.transfer`
   - `invocation`: canonical example, e.g. `btcli wallet transfer --destination 5G... --amount 1.0 --no-prompt`
   - `args`: array of {name, type, required, default, description}
   - `read_or_write`: `read` | `write` | `mixed`
   - `extrinsic`: pallet + dispatchable, e.g. `Balances.transfer_keep_alive`, or `null` for read-only.
   - `storage_keys`: list of subtensor storage keys read/written, best effort.
   - `events_expected`: list of events the extrinsic should emit (read from `subtensor/pallets/`).
   - `source_file_ref`: path:line inside the locally-installed bittensor-cli package (`.venv/lib/python3.x/site-packages/bittensor_cli/...`) that handles this subcommand.
   - `notes`: anything operator-relevant.
2. `docs/parity/inventory-btcli.md` — human-readable view rendered from the JSON: grouped by top-level command (wallet / subnet / stake / sudo / root / weights / view / config / utils / liveness / etc.), each row a one-line summary + a link to the JSON entry.

Methodology:
- Activate venv: `source .venv/bin/activate`.
- Walk the help tree non-interactively: `btcli --help`, then for each top-level group `btcli <group> --help`, then for each leaf `btcli <group> <cmd> --help`. Many help texts are paginated through `rich`; pipe through `cat` or set `--no-color` if needed.
- For each leaf, open the corresponding source file in `.venv/lib/.../bittensor_cli/` and confirm the extrinsic call (search for `substrate.compose_call`, `subtensor.set_weights`, `add_stake`, etc.). Record the substrate pallet + dispatchable.
- Cross-reference each extrinsic with `subtensor/pallets/<pallet>/src/lib.rs` (or `macros/dispatches.rs`) to record the canonical event names emitted.
- For commands that wrap multiple extrinsics (e.g. `wallet create` issues `new_coldkey` + `new_hotkey`), record all of them in a single row's `extrinsic` field as an array.
- Mark dry-run-only / preview commands as `read`.
- For commands that have been split or renamed across btcli versions, record only the version pinned in `docs/parity/versions.json`.

Do NOT touch agcli source, tests, or other parity-matrix files. Your output is exclusively the two `inventory-btcli` files.

If a btcli command appears completely undocumented in source, mark `extrinsic: "UNKNOWN"` and explain in `notes`.
acceptance: `docs/parity/inventory-btcli.json` is a syntactically valid JSON array (verify with `jq type`).
Every top-level btcli command group appears (`wallet`, `subnet`, `stake`, `sudo`, `root`, `weights`, `view`, `config`, `utils`, `liveness`, `info` — whichever groups exist in the pinned version).
Every leaf has `id`, `invocation`, `args`, `read_or_write`, and either `extrinsic` set or a `notes` justification for `null`.
Every `write` row has a non-null `extrinsic`.
`docs/parity/inventory-btcli.md` renders the same data grouped by top-level command, with each row linking to its `id` in the JSON.
tasks.verify:
## Automated
- `jq -e 'type == "array" and length > 20' docs/parity/inventory-btcli.json`.
- `jq -e 'all(.[]; .id and .invocation and .read_or_write and (.read_or_write != "write" or .extrinsic != null))' docs/parity/inventory-btcli.json`.
- Spot-check 5 random rows by running their `invocation` with `--help` to confirm the args exist.

tasks.name: inventory-sdk
tasks.scopedGoal:
Phase 1 — Exhaustive enumeration of chain-relevant Bittensor Python SDK helpers for the parity matrix.

Read `.orchestrate/agcli-parity/discovery.md` and the upstream `bootstrap-parity-env` handoff FIRST. The `.venv/` already has `bittensor` installed.

Deliverables:

1. `docs/parity/inventory-sdk.json` — array of rows, one per chain-relevant SDK helper. Each row:
   - `id`: e.g. `sdk.async_subtensor.transfer` or `sdk.async_subtensor.add_stake`.
   - `module`: import path (e.g. `bittensor.core.async_subtensor`).
   - `function`: function or method name.
   - `signature`: canonical Python signature.
   - `read_or_write`: `read` | `write`.
   - `extrinsic`: pallet + dispatchable, or `null` for read-only.
   - `storage_keys`: list of storage keys read/written.
   - `events_expected`: list of events expected on write.
   - `source_file_ref`: path:line inside the locally-installed bittensor package.
   - `notes`.
2. `docs/parity/inventory-sdk.md` — grouped human view (extrinsic-submitter group vs read-helper group vs subtensor-runtime-api group).

Methodology:
- Inspect `.venv/lib/python3.x/site-packages/bittensor/` (recursive).
- Focus on **chain-relevant** helpers: things that issue an extrinsic via `substrate.compose_call` / `substrate.create_signed_extrinsic` (writes), things that call `substrate.query` / `substrate.query_map` / `query_runtime_api` (reads), and things that wrap multiple of those.
- Out of scope: Axon/Dendrite HTTP servers, neuron classes, miner runtime helpers, Synapse classes, wallet keyfile handling unrelated to chain ops, logging utilities.
- Include `subtensor.SubtensorInterface` / `async_subtensor.AsyncSubtensor` methods, the `bittensor.Subtensor` legacy class methods that wrap extrinsics, and the runtime-api wrappers in `bittensor.core.chain_data`/`runtime_api`.
- Cross-reference each extrinsic with `subtensor/pallets/<pallet>/` for the dispatchable + event names.
- For helpers that map to the same dispatchable (e.g. `subtensor.transfer` and `async_subtensor.transfer`), record both rows but cross-link them via `notes: "async pair of sdk.subtensor.transfer"`.

Do NOT touch agcli source, tests, or other parity-matrix files. Your output is exclusively the two `inventory-sdk` files.

tasks.name: parity-matrix
tasks.scopedGoal:
Phase 2 — Build the agcli parity matrix joining `inventory-btcli`, `inventory-sdk`, and the current agcli command surface.

Read `.orchestrate/agcli-parity/discovery.md` and the upstream `inventory-btcli` and `inventory-sdk` handoffs FIRST. Treat their JSON outputs as the canonical input.

Also read the agcli surface from:
- `src/cli/mod.rs` (the 28 `*Commands` enums; ~3204 LOC).
- `docs/llm.txt` (agent-facing reference card).
- `docs/commands/*.md` (per-group reference; produced by the prior `agcli-audit` orchestrate run).
- `docs/why-agcli.md` (claimed parity & superset).

Deliverables:

1. `docs/parity/matrix.json` — array of rows. Schema (also documented in `.orchestrate/agcli-parity/discovery.md` under `Matrix row schema`):
   - `id`: stable id — `btcli.<group>.<cmd>` or `sdk.<module>.<fn>` or `agcli.<group>.<cmd>` (the last for agcli-unique rows).
   - `source`: `btcli` | `sdk` | `agcli-unique`.
   - `ref_invocation`: canonical btcli/SDK invocation (null for `agcli-unique`).
   - `ref_extrinsic`: pallet.dispatchable (null for reads or agcli-unique).
   - `agcli_invocation`: canonical agcli invocation (null for `GAP`).
   - `agcli_status`: one of `COVERED_E2E` | `COVERED_CLI_ONLY` | `COVERED_UNIQUE` | `GAP` | `N/A`.
   - `agcli_flag_diffs`: array of `"btcli: <old> ↔ agcli: <new>"` strings (empty for `agcli-unique` and `GAP`).
   - `parity_test`: null at this phase (Phase 3 fills it in).
   - `notes`: free text.
2. `docs/parity/matrix.md` — grouped human view: by phase target (Phase 3 candidates = `COVERED_CLI_ONLY` + `COVERED_UNIQUE`; Phase 4 candidates = `GAP`; informational = `COVERED_E2E` + `N/A`).

Policy for assigning `agcli_status`:
- `COVERED_CLI_ONLY` — agcli has the command surface but no `tests/parity/` test yet. Default for almost every row at this phase since Phase 3 hasn't run.
- `COVERED_E2E` — set ONLY when an existing test under `tests/` (e.g. `tests/e2e_test.rs`, `tests/user_flows_e2e.rs`, `tests/audit_<group>.rs`) already exercises the operation end-to-end against localnet. Cite the test path:test_name in `notes`.
- `COVERED_UNIQUE` — for rows where the matrix `source` is `agcli-unique` (agcli has something btcli/SDK does not — examples in `docs/why-agcli.md`).
- `GAP` — agcli has no command and no obvious way to express the operation.
- `N/A` — explicitly out of scope per the mission (Axon/Dendrite HTTP runtime, Yuma math internals, subnet-specific scoring). Record the justification in `notes`.

Methodology:
- Start from `docs/parity/inventory-btcli.json` and `docs/parity/inventory-sdk.json`. Iterate.
- For each row, search `src/cli/mod.rs` and `docs/llm.txt` for the equivalent agcli surface. Use `rg` heavily.
- For each agcli-unique command in `docs/why-agcli.md` under "unique to agcli" sections, add an `agcli-unique` row.
- When btcli and SDK rows map to the same on-chain dispatchable, link them in `notes` but keep distinct rows (their UX criteria are tested separately in Phase 3).

Do NOT modify the upstream inventories or any source file. Your output is exclusively `docs/parity/matrix.{json,md}`.
acceptance: `docs/parity/matrix.json` valid JSON array with every row from `inventory-btcli.json` and `inventory-sdk.json` represented at least once (count check).
Every row has an `agcli_status` in {COVERED_E2E, COVERED_CLI_ONLY, COVERED_UNIQUE, GAP, N/A}.
Every `N/A` row has a non-empty `notes`.
Every `agcli-unique` row appears in `docs/why-agcli.md` (cite location).
`docs/parity/matrix.md` lists Phase 3 candidates and Phase 4 candidates separately.

- `jq -e '[.[] | select(.source == "btcli")] | length == ([inputs[] | select(.source == "btcli")] | length)' docs/parity/matrix.json docs/parity/inventory-btcli.json` (or equivalent count match).

tasks.name: phase3-parity-suite
tasks.scopedGoal:
Phase 3 — Build a localnet parity test suite (`tests/parity/`) that, for every row in `docs/parity/matrix.json` with `agcli_status` in {COVERED_CLI_ONLY, COVERED_UNIQUE, COVERED_E2E}, runs the reference command (btcli or SDK) and the agcli equivalent against the same fresh localnet and asserts equivalent on-chain effects (storage / events / balances / stake / weights / hyperparams).

Read `.orchestrate/agcli-parity/discovery.md`, the upstream `parity-matrix` handoff, and `tests/e2e_modules/harness.rs` BEFORE publishing any tasks.

Your scope as a subplanner: decompose by command category (each category becomes one worker), spawn the workers, collect their handoffs, then aggregate into a single subplanner handoff for the root. Categories (one parity worker per category):

1. `parity-balance-transfer` — `btcli wallet transfer` / `transfer_all` / `transfer_keep_alive` + sdk equivalents vs `agcli transfer*`, `agcli balance`.
2. `parity-wallet` — wallet create/list/show/regen/derive/dev-key/associate-hotkey/check-swap/show-mnemonic + sdk equivalents vs `agcli wallet *`.
3. `parity-stake-basic` — add_stake / remove_stake / add_stake_limit / remove_stake_limit / unstake_all + sdk vs `agcli stake *`.
